2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
That on 13.03.2024 at 06.00 AM., he was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HK-2652, in 14 th cross, 11th main junction, Jayanagar 5th block,

sentences.text: Petitioner was shifted to Sri.Krishna Sevashrama Hospital, wherein he took first aid, later he was shifted to Rajashekara Multi specialty Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for the accidental injuries and he has spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards his medical expenses.
He stated that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to perform his work as earlier.
Prior to the accident the he was hale and healthy and he is aged about 44 years and he is working in BBMP and he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

Further petitioner stated that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle which belongs to respondent and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.31/2024 against the driver of the offending BMTC bus, as such respondent is liable to pay the compensation.
He prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondent, he appeared through their/its counsel and filed vakalath, written statement by denying the entire version of the petitioner in toto.

Respondent specifically denied the age, income and profession of the petitioner and contended that the alleged incident had occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and prays this court to dismiss the petition.
4. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined the medical record keeper and doctor as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 21 documents, which are at Ex.P.1 to 21 and they are fully cross examined.
Respondent examined the driver of the offending vehicle as RW-1, he is fully cross examined.
5. I have heard the arguments for the counsels appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

6. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 13.03.2024 at 06.00 AM., he was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05- HK-2652, in 14th cross, 11th main junction, Jayanagar 5th block, Bangalore, along with Harisha as a pillion rider, wherein the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg No.KA-57-F-4586 drove it with speed,
rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the vehicle and caused the accident and thereby Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the said accident?
Harijana Anjinappa vs B.M.T.C on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10336619/
2 2)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether respondent proves that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the negligent act of the rider as contended at para No.5 of the written statement ?
3) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4) What order or award?
7.

After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue no.2: In the Negative,
 Issue no.3: In partly affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 8. Issue No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, sketch, mahazar, IMV report, final report, MLC register, intimation to the police, which are at Ex.P.1 to 4, 6 & 7, 15 & 16.
9.

On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that one Omnkarappa S/o Channappa was the driver of the offending BMTC bus and the accident took place due to his rash and negligent act.

Further Ex.P.5 is the wound certificate, Ex.P8 & 9 is the discharge summary, it reveals that the petitioner has sustained the grievous head injuries that is left frontal and right temporal contusions and acute sub dural Hemotoma, and he has taken treatment as an inpatient for 7 days in Rajashekara Multi specialty Hospital and he was discharged on 21.03.2024 and he has spent Rs.98,362/- for his medical expenses as per Ex.P.12.
10.

In the cross examination of the PW-1 he clearly denied the entire version of the respondent in toto and nothing worth has been elicited to probabilise the alleged negligent act on the part of the petitioner.
In the cross examination of RW-1, he admitted that final report is filed against him as per Ex.P.7 and he has not lodged separate complaint against the petitioner.

He further he admitted the details of damages of the Bus as stated in IMV report which is at Ex.P.6.
11.
The aforesaid fact falsifies the entire contention of the respondent and fortifies the petitioner allegations.
Accordingly respondent version cannot be accepted.
Respondent has not challenged the final report which is at Ex.P.7 and it is filed after through investigation and it cannot be ignored as it has reached the finalty.
Inasmuch respondent version cannot accepted without any tantamount evidence.

sentences.text:
Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:

Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary, which are Ex.P 5 and 8, the entry there in reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous head injuries that is left frontal and right temporal contusions and acute sub dural Hemotoma and he took treatment as inpatient for 7 days and he was discharged on 21.03.2024 and he has spent Rs.98,362/- for his medical expenses as per Ex.P.12.
Further for attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, she might have spend some more amount.
Therefore, in addition actual medical expenses of Rs.98,362/-, I award Rs.20,000/- and petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,18,362/-, compensation under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
13. The petitioner has not substantiated his nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place in the year 2024, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2024 is Rs.16,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least one month, he has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.16,500/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
14. The petitioner has examined the doctor Dr.Shailesh.A.V, working as neurosurgeon as PW-3.
He deposed that he has not treated the petitioner and petitioner has 15% of whole body disability and petitioner has taken conservative treatment.

He further deposed that wounds are not yet healed and he has conducted Indian disability evaluation and assessment score for the petitioner and petitioner is having disability and it is permanent in nature.
15. I have perused the evidence of PW-3 wound certificate, discharge summary, and reports and it corroborates with oral testimony of PW-3.
Nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW-3 to disprove the said medical investigation and his report.
It is true that petitioner has physical disability due to accidental injuries.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity due to accidental injuries is different from the percentage of physical disability due to accidental injuries.
Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 15%.
16. The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.16,500/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 43 years as per the entry in Aadhar card which is at Ex P.10.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "14".
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.4,15,800/- as compensation under this head.
